_comment: S17 / brief criterion 7 — the retrieval smoke set.
14 queries across Trane Precedent and Carrier 48/50 faults, phrased the way a
technician would type them rather than the way a manual is indexed. The bar is
at least 10 of 12 returning the correct document, with the page correct on
those 10 — 14 are listed so the bar survives two being wrong for reasons that
turn out to be about the corpus rather than about retrieval.
HOW A QUERY IS JUDGED
expectDocs   — regexes against the document label. A hit on ANY of them is a
correct document. Several faults are legitimately covered by
more than one manual in this corpus, and insisting on one
specific file would measure luck rather than retrieval.
expectTerms  — terms that must appear in the retrieved chunk's text for the
PAGE to count as correct. This is what makes page-correctness
machine-checkable: a chunk from the right document but the
wrong page will not contain them. It is a necessary condition,
not a sufficient one — a human still confirms the page says
what the answer will claim, which is Stage 5.5's job.
Expectations are written against documents that are actually in the corpus.
Trane Foundation is deliberately absent: RT-SVX096C is a dead URL and the gap
is recorded in 00-brief.md Amendment 2. Do not add a Foundation query here to
make coverage look complete.
